newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says China shows progress on human rights.
newsitem.headline: France says China shows progress on human rights.

text.p: France, noting what it described as progress by China on human rights, said on Friday it would not sponsor a resolution on the issue at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva.
The announcement precedes a trip to China due in mid-May by President Jacques Chirac, who on Thursday met visiting senior Chinese politburo member Qiao Shi who in Paris.
"France has decided not to sponsor the plan for a resolution on human rights in China. There has been progress on three points," French foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

He said that Chinese leaders had "announced their readiness to sign the two U.N. 1996 pacts" on human rights and that "relations have been established between China and the International (Committee of the) Red Cross".
In addition, the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and the rapporteur of the Geneva-based commission have just been invited to visit China, Rummelhardt said.

Every year since the army's crushing of pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiannamen Square in June, 1989, the European Union has put forward a resolution criticising human rights violations in China to the commission.

But China has so far escaped official condemnation by mustering enough support despite pressure from Europeans, the United States and other western states. The EU is this year divided on whether to put foward such a resolution.

Rummelhardt said that a change in the Chinese penal code was under way and that the country was living through a period of transition following the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on February 19.
"In this difficult phase, we will not take the road of confrontation," said Rummelhardt, who acknowledged that progress still had to be made and this would take time.
Qiao Shi, head of China's National People's Congress, said after meeting Chirac that the French head of state's trip should lay the groundwork for a "new Spring" for Sino-French relations.
James Sasser, U.S. ambassador to China, said on Thursday he expected Washington to ask the U.N. rights commission to adopt a resolution criticising China for human rights abuses.
